title: How to Move up to the Next Level: Mastery & Masterminds
overview: Vishen explains why Mindvalley is opening up the methods it once reserved for a handful of hand-picked authors, and walks you through the two ways to keep working with him: the Expert to Authority Mastery and an application-only mastermind for experts already earning six figures. Along the way you get genuine teaching on the belief that authority is a replicable method, the 'done or not done' operating mindset, recent conversion discoveries, and a live demonstration of building an autoresponder with a trained AI.
key_ideas: Mindvalley used to receive around 3,000 author applications a year and choose five. Vishen's new strategy for reaching a billion people is to open up the methodology, webinar system and tools rather than work with authors one at a time.

Adopt the belief that authority is a replicable method. It is not talent or luck; Vishen has run the same process for over 100 authors, and when you know the method, authority becomes predictable rather than something you hope for.

You have to solve two problems at once: articulate what you do (phraseology, sequence and teaching technique applied as a science, as with the naming of Regan Hillyer's method and Bert Goldman's Quantum Jumping) and be findable. You do not need a marketing degree; you need the framework and the right AI and marketing tools.

Precision beats improvisation. The webinar template shared with students is 56 pages and has been refined since 2008 with input from the people who invented the telesummit and wrote the book on webinars; with AI trained on an author's course, a script that once took days now takes about two hours.

A recent test found a masterclass with only the ums and ahs cut out beat the heavily edited version by 30% in revenue. Vishen's read: fancy edits feel like an ad, simple edits feel real, and publishing the next day instead of 20 days later matters more than polish.

Ban 'I'm currently doing' from your vocabulary. In Vishen's company work is either done or not done, a signature method or a script is built in one day and then improved, and the goal is massive results in the least time rather than hustle.

A business grows through three stages: do it yourself, optimise it, automate it. Once you reach automation, you are assembling bricks that connect, and Vishen expects most students to end up with a three- or four-day work week while revenue rises.

Everyone is now a media company of one. The method works for physical products, supplements, software and B2B as well as courses; only the platform and tone shift (LinkedIn rather than Instagram for B2B). What does not change is that you, the founder, must be the spokesperson rather than staying behind the curtain.

Your first niche may fail and that is fine. Vishen's first attempt was selling stuffed toys; once you own the method you can point it at another niche. The mental frame matters as much as the method: with 'everything is figureoutable', a roadblock is just a sequence to work out.

Give the AI the context and it does the heavy lifting: an audience brief built from your survey answers, a training file on the discipline (for example autoresponder design) and a transcript of your book or best talk produce a finished 10- to 14-day sequence in minutes. Ask it clarifying questions rather than just issuing orders.

frameworks.name: The two problems behind the authority gap
steps: Articulate what you do: name your method, sequence your teaching, make it sticky for the student
Be findable: social, ads, webinars, quizzes and email sequences that put you in front of the market
Solve both at once using the framework plus the right AI and marketing tools, not a marketing degree

frameworks.name: Three stages of building the business
steps: Do it yourself: understand the principle and produce the first version
Optimise it: build a trained AI project that improves with every correction
Automate it: connect the pieces so the business runs and scales without you in the room

frameworks.name: Implementation lab protocol (as demonstrated)
steps: The teaching call sets out the principle, for example autoresponder design
A facilitator turns the lesson into an implementation protocol and training files (MD and skill files) for your AI
You install the files, complete a questionnaire and upload your own material (book transcript, best speech, audience brief)
The AI asks clarifying questions (length, number of close emails, which product) and produces the finished asset
You paste the output into your own system; the asset is ready the same week

frameworks.name: Five pillars and milestones of the curriculum
steps: Messaging and positioning (weeks 1 to 4, Daniel Priestley on high-value signature offers in week 3)
Platform and content
Funnel and conversion (by week 10, designing expert funnels with the five stages of funnel design and lead magnets)
Scale and products (week 14, high-ticket mastery: selling $3,000 to $10,000 programmes)
Legacy and systems (week 17 collaborative partnerships and affiliates; week 18 legacy and impact)

frameworks.name: How the expert mastermind shares knowledge
steps: A capped group of about 90 experts, by application
Each member commits to sharing one test, idea or new insight every month
Across 90 members that yields roughly three insights a day
Vishen adds one advanced lesson a month drawn from what is working across the Mindvalley ecosystem

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: Authority is not talent, it's not luck, it's a method. Authority is a method.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: Why I think this happens is I think when people see fancy edits, it feels like an ad, but if they see a simple edit, it feels real.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: It's either not done or it's done. And I train everyone in my team to build lightning fast and develop it in one day.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: All of us are a media company of one. You're the media company for your product.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: I hate being busy. I hate overwork. In fact, I just don't like work at all. I want to get massive results in the least amount of time.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Is this for me if I'm just starting?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Yes. The one thing you must have is some idea of the niche you want to try first; it can be vague, and it does not have to be the final one. My first niche was stuffed toys and it failed, but once you learn the system you can try it on a different niche.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Does it work if I'm not selling courses or coaching?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Nora sells gut-health testing kits; you can use a webinar, an autoresponder or a quiz to sell a physical product, a supplement, a medical service or software. The key is that we are teaching you to be the spokesperson, the known scientist in your field, not to stay behind the curtain.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: I've tried building an audience before and it did not work. Why would this be different?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Ask whether you had the right methodology, the right tools, the right allies and the right mental frame. Many people's first thought is 'I'm going to hit a roadblock', so they never try; if you go in believing everything is figureoutable, every roadblock is just a sequence to work out. I'll work with you on both the method and the frame.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: What happens after the 18 weeks?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: You stay in a community that remains active and supportive. Everyone is on the app, and every member who gives permission can chat with every other member, which in itself is incredibly valuable.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Neelia asks whether you still have access to all the templates after the four months are up.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Yes, you do.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Sabine says marketing is her weak spot: she has programmes and frameworks but not the team or tools to get a breakthrough. Will the Mastery help with that?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Yes. It has never been easier to set up an authority company of one, and you rarely need to hire. You need to know either the easiest tool for a landing page, quiz or masterclass, or which agency can do it in two or three days at minimal cost, and in the programme we share our favourite tools and experts.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Shami: most programmes like this are B2C. My business is B2B management, reporting and optimisation. Will it work?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: A large chunk of our previous Mastery students were B2B, and Mindvalley itself sells to corporations and governments. The method is the same; what shifts is the platform (LinkedIn rather than Instagram) and the tone and style of communication.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Is this useful for Jovi, a verified-safe makeup brand for kids?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Yes, because you are talking to the parents, and as a parent I immediately ask whether this is safe for my daughter. What is missing from the site is the story and the founder: is that photo the founder or stock photography? Where is the name and the signature? For a controversial product, how you present it decides whether it takes off.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Carolina: I'm still developing my offer, positioning, signature method and case studies. Is this designed to build them from scratch?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: You build them from scratch, and you build them in one day. There is no 'I'm currently doing' in my company; it is done or not done. We give you the method, the AI tool and the system, so you have a ready-to-go signature method on your website in a day, then adapt it as you learn.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Diana: how exactly does the guidance work for building out systems and frameworks?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: I or Daniel teach on Tuesday; a facilitator turns that into an implementation protocol and training files for your AI; on Friday you install them, fill in a questionnaire, upload your book transcript or best speech, and the AI produces the finished asset. I'm building a 14-day autoresponder live right now in about five minutes, something that took me a week last year.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Judy: my husband and I are co-founders. Can we attend under one enrolment?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: It's tricky because every student has one profile in the directory, like a university. I've asked my team to set up a discount for genuine business partners and spouses.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Paula: how long is the AI available to you?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: For the four months, and you can download the content as MD files and put it into your own AI. You control it and there is nothing you are locked into.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Linda: I did Entrepreneurship Mastery last year. Should I join this one, and how does it differ from Social Media Mastery?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: There is some overlap with Entrepreneurship Mastery, so previous students will be contacted about a discount for that overlap. Social Media Mastery is completely different: that is reels and charisma; this is platform, structure, marketing and product design.

programme_summary: Vishen restated the Expert to Authority Mastery: four months (October to January), 18 weeks, 36 live sessions covering 18 topics, with a 90-minute teaching call and a 60-minute implementation lab on Fridays at 9am Los Angeles / 12pm New York / 6pm Amsterdam / 8pm Dubai / 9.30pm Delhi / midnight Singapore, recorded, with roughly three further hours a week suggested for implementation. He teaches about two-thirds of it, with Daniel Priestley, Jimmy Naraine, John Lee and Ajit Nawalkha as guest teachers and periodic appearances from Mindvalley authors; each student receives a companion AI (cost covered for the four months, content downloadable afterwards) and access to the premium community. The kickoff is a 'Build Your AI Intelligence' skill-pack session with Vishen on Friday 25 September, for which an AI subscription (Claude, ChatGPT or similar) is required. Stated price: $4,999, or $1,499 over four months, with Mindvalley members paying $4,499, and a one-click full refund available at any time in the first two weeks; those enrolling by 11.59pm Los Angeles on Monday 21 September were offered a flagship-course workshop with Jimmy Naraine. Vishen also announced an application-only mastermind (referred to on Day 2 as the Expert Guild) for experts earning at least $100,000 a year from their own teaching or spokesperson role: about 90 members, each sharing one test or insight a month, plus a monthly advanced lesson from Vishen and participation from Mindvalley authors, priced at $10,000, or $12,000 combined with the Mastery, with details to follow by email and a dedicated presentation later in the week.
next_steps: Write down the belief 'authority is a replicable method' and list the specific things currently stopping you (mindset, phraseology, no flagship course, funnel, masterclass, quiz or email sequence).
Pick one asset you have been 'currently doing' and finish a first version of it in a single day, then improve it from there.
Check your own product page for founder visibility: your name, your face, your signature and your story should be unmistakable.

If you are considering the programme, download the full week-by-week overview that was shared, confirm you have an AI subscription, and decide whether the Mastery or the application-only mastermind fits your current revenue.
attribution_notes: Lines are labelled 'Vishen' and 'Mindvalley' (Jason Goldberg), so attribution is high confidence. In the Q&A portion Vishen read most audience questions himself from a slide and later from his own screen, so those are attributed to 'Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)' rather than to Jason, who relayed only the first two. Names corrected from the transcription: Reagan/Reagan Hiller = Regan Hillyer, Marisa Pierre/Pia = Marisa Peer, Jimmy Noreen/Nuraid/Durain = Jimmy Naraine, Arjit Nawalka = Ajit Nawalkha, Marie Folio = Marie Forleo, Alex Mendozian = Alex Mandossian, Jason Flatline = Jason Fladlien; team members named on stage are described by role only.
